title: Class hierarchy
summary: Explore how Retiam’s classes and interfaces relate, then open a type’s API to inspect its behavior.

blocks.text: Start with Entity to see the scene-node family. Focus on VectorEntity to follow vector geometry, or switch to Animation to explore timing and motion. Choose how many descendant levels to show; ancestors stay visible so you can see where the selected type fits. The index includes documented engine and library classes and interfaces, including types with no descendants.

cells: Scene nodes: cameras, geometry, groups and nested scenes. Follow VectorEntity to the vector-shape branches.
Timing and choreography. Follow StateAnimation for state changes, Sequential for sequences, and Concurrent for simultaneous animation.
Geometry, shading, rendering, interaction, audio and physics attached to entities.
Frame-graph work: rendering, compute, post-processing and presentation.
Classes implementing the plugin contract. Dashed arrows identify implementation rather than inheritance.

blocks.text: A solid arrow from Entity to Camera means Camera extends Entity. An italic label marks an abstract class, such as Animation or Component. Interface boxes have dashed borders; enabling interface implementations adds dashed arrows from a contract to the classes that implement it. Interface-to-interface inheritance uses solid arrows.

These connections come from TypeScript heritage declarations, resolved through the compiler’s symbols. Imported aliases and generic base types keep their actual declaration targets. New documented classes appear when the documentation is rebuilt; diagram nodes and the list below them link to the same API anchors as the rest of the site.

The scene graph’s parent/child links describe ownership between instances. This diagram describes relationships between types. Consult [entities and ownership](/entities) for scene composition, and inspect each base type’s API for inherited behavior.

A dimmed node is a base declaration outside the API index. It supplies inheritance context and has no API link. Type aliases and utility types used in heritage declarations appear as contracts with dashed borders. Factory functions and structural compatibility do not create additional inheritance edges.
